title: Spectrum after inverting the regular elements on a finite closed-fibre module
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, where $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A$ (every element outside $\mathfrak m_A$ is a unit). Let $N$ be a $B$-module. Put $C=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ and $\overline N=N/\mathfrak m_AN$, with the induced $C$-module structure. Suppose $C$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\overline N$ is a finite $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let
$$\Sigma=\{b\in B:\overline N\xrightarrow{z\mapsto bz}\overline N\text{ is injective}\}.$$
This is a multiplicative subset, and write $\Sigma^{-1}B$ for the ring of fractions $b/s$, $s\in\Sigma$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Use exact element-annihilator associated primes [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], viewing $\overline N$ also as a $B$-module through $B\to C$. Contraction along $B\to\Sigma^{-1}B$ identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(\Sigma^{-1}B)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with precisely the primes $\mathfrak p\subset B$ contained in some $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(\overline N)$. The ring $\Sigma^{-1}B$ is semilocal, meaning that it has finitely many maximal ideals, and the contractions of its maximal ideals are exactly the maximal elements, under inclusion, of $\operatorname{Ass}_B(\overline N)$. In particular each maximal ideal contracts to the inverse image of an associated prime of $\overline N$ over $C$. The zero module is allowed; then $\Sigma=B$, the localization is the zero ring, and its spectrum and set of maximal ideals are empty.

proof.text: Write $I=\mathfrak m_AB$, $M=\overline N$, and $\pi:B\to C=B/I$. The identity acts injectively on $M$, and a composite of two injective scalar maps is injective, so $1\in\Sigma$ and $\Sigma\Sigma\subseteq\Sigma$. For every $z\in M$ one has $\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)=\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{Ann}_C(z))$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_C(z)=\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)/I$. Surjectivity of $\pi$ gives a bijection between these annihilators, and preserves and reflects primality: a product of classes kills $z$ precisely when the product of any lifts does, and properness is equivalent to $1$ not killing $z$. Thus $\operatorname{Ass}_B(M)=\{\pi^{-1}(Q):Q\in\operatorname{Ass}_C(M)\}$, with injective indexing, by the exact-annihilator definition. This writes out the quotient-ring comparison in Tag 05BY (lemma-ass-quotient-ring).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite] to the Noetherian ring $C$ and its finite module $M$. It gives finiteness of $\operatorname{Ass}_C(M)$, hence of $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{Ass}_B(M)$ by step 1. No Noetherianity of $B$ is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 05DE (lemma-homothety-spectrum), proof, finiteness sentence using algebra.tex Tag 00LC (lemma-finite-ass).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-module-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes] over $C$ to $M$. Multiplication by $b$ on $M$ fails to be injective exactly when some nonzero $z$ has $bz=0$, exactly when $\pi(b)$ lies in an associated prime of $M$ over $C$. Taking inverse images and using step 1 gives $B\setminus\Sigma=\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\in\mathcal Q}\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 05DE (lemma-homothety-spectrum), proof, complement formula using algebra.tex Tag 00LD (lemma-ass-zero-divisors).

proof.text: Set $T=\Sigma^{-1}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding], contraction identifies $\operatorname{Spec}T$ with the primes $\mathfrak p$ of $B$ disjoint from $\Sigma$. By step 3, disjointness is equivalent to $\mathfrak p\subseteq\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\in\mathcal Q}\mathfrak q$. If $\mathcal Q$ is nonempty, the finite prime-avoidance statement [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] applies to the ideal $\mathfrak p$ and this finite family of prime ideals, and makes this equivalent to $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$ for some $\mathfrak q\in\mathcal Q$. If $\mathcal Q$ is empty, no ideal is contained in its empty union, since every ideal contains $0$; both conditions are false. Conversely any prime contained in a member of $\mathcal Q$ is disjoint from $\Sigma$ by step 3. This proves the stated spectrum description.

source.place: Tag 05DE (lemma-homothety-spectrum), proof, prime correspondence using algebra.tex Tags 00E3 (lemma-spec-localization) and 00DS (lemma-silly).

proof.text: For every ideal $J\subseteq T$ and $a\in B$, $s\in\Sigma$, one has $a/s\in J$ if and only if $a/1\in J$: multiply by the unit $s/1$ or its inverse $1/s$. Hence an ideal of $T$ is determined by its contraction and inclusions of ideals are reflected by contraction. In particular, if $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is the unique prime over $\mathfrak q\in\mathcal Q$ supplied by step 4, then $a/s\in P_{\mathfrak q}$ if and only if $a\in\mathfrak q$, and $P_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq P_{\mathfrak r}$ if and only if $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak r$.

source.place: Tag 05DE (lemma-homothety-spectrum), proof, last paragraph; fraction operations in algebra.tex Tag 00CO (definition-localization).

proof.text: Every proper ideal $J\subset T$ is contained in some $P_{\mathfrak q}$. Indeed, its contraction $K$ misses $\Sigma$, since $J$ contains no unit. By step 3, $K\subseteq\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\in\mathcal Q}\mathfrak q$; this forces $\mathcal Q$ nonempty because $0\in K$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] to $K$ to get $K\subseteq\mathfrak q$, and step 5 gives $J\subseteq P_{\mathfrak q}$. Now a maximal ideal $J$ must equal this proper prime $P_{\mathfrak q}$, and $\mathfrak q$ must be maximal in $\mathcal Q$, since a strictly larger member would give a strictly larger proper prime by step 5. Conversely, if $\mathfrak q$ is maximal in $\mathcal Q$ and $J$ is a proper ideal containing $P_{\mathfrak q}$, choose $\mathfrak r\in\mathcal Q$ with $J\subseteq P_{\mathfrak r}$. Contraction gives $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak r$, so $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak r$ and $J=P_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is maximal. This proves the exact maximal-ideal assertion without presupposing a theorem on existence of maximal ideals. Finiteness in step 2 makes $T$ semilocal, and step 1 identifies each contracted maximal ideal with the inverse image of an associated prime over $C$.

source.place: Tag 05DE (lemma-homothety-spectrum), proof, last paragraph; algebra.tex Tag 00DS (lemma-silly) applied to the contraction of any proper ideal.

proof.text: If $M=0$, every scalar map on $M$ is injective, so $\Sigma=B$; no element of $M$ has a proper annihilator, so its associated-prime set is empty. The fraction relation with denominator set $B$ gives $1/1=0/1$ (take the annihilating factor $0\in\Sigma$). Thus $T$ is the zero ring and has no proper ideal, hence no prime or maximal ideal. All conclusions above include this case.
